title: POOL_SIZE is compile-time only: WC_HW_E misleadingly looks like hardware failure
description:
Scenario: A TLS server with more than WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_POOL_SIZE=8 concurrent in-flight AES-GCM records gets WC_HW_E from crypto2dev_pool_acquire. This propagates up as a wolfSSL record-layer error, which looks like hardware failure or a broken connection. The error message is 'crypto2dev: cipher pool exhausted'.

Users who see WC_HW_E on a loaded server will assume hardware is broken and open a support issue before reading the pool size comments.

The fix (increase WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_POOL_SIZE and recompile) is correct, but requiring recompilation to tune for concurrency level is surprising for a library.

A runtime-configurable pool size (passed to wc_crypto2dev_init(int pool_size)) would let the user set it once in their initialization code. This is an API-breaking change now if added later.

Decision point: Should wc_crypto2dev_init() accept a pool_size parameter now, before this API fossilizes?
